title: DIRECT: When and Where Should You Allocate Test-Time Compute in Embodied Planners?
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed as high-level planners for embodied agents, with an emerging strategy of scaling test-time compute to improve capability. However, we observe that doing so increases latency, token usage, and FLOPs while yielding uneven, often diminishing gains in downstream success, limiting where embodied agents can be deployed. We argue that choosing when and where to spend test-time compute is central to bringing frontier performance to the real world. We introduce DIRECT, a routing framework that uses multimodal scene context to allocate compute per prompt, improving the success--cost Pareto frontier over fixed model selection. Across three dominant scaling axes, namely chain-of-thought depth, model size, and memory history, our experiments on VLABench and RoboMME show that test-time compute is not a uniform lever: different axes yield qualitatively distinct capability gains. We validate these insights on a physical Franka arm in a DROID setup spanning zero-shot manipulation and long-horizon chaining, where our router matches or exceeds a stronger model's success rate at up to 65% lower average latency. Ultimately, our results show that naively scaling test-time compute is wasteful, and that DIRECT can provide frontier-level embodied planning in robotic systems at a fraction of the cost. Project page can be found at jadee-dao.github.io/direct/.

significance.justification: The paper directly changes a core decision for builders deploying VLMs as planners by introducing a routing framework that optimizes the success-cost Pareto frontier, showing up to 65% lower latency while matching stronger models.

novelty.justification: It introduces a novel routing framework, DIRECT, that uses multimodal scene context to dynamically allocate test-time compute across different scaling axes, a substantial new variation distinct from prior fixed compute approaches.

reproducibility.justification: The paper provides a project page and states experiments were conducted on public benchmarks (VLABench, RoboMME) and a physical Franka arm setup, indicating code and clear instructions are likely public.

clarity.justification: The abstract is well-written, clearly states the problem of uneven gains from scaling test-time compute, proposes the DIRECT solution, and presents specific, measurable results across multiple axes and benchmarks.

topical_fit.justification: The paper is directly in the applied-AI sweet spot, focusing on optimizing Vision-Language Model deployment for embodied agents, a core concern for engineers building real-world LLM systems.

sections.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed as high-level planners for embodied agents, with an emerging strategy of scaling test-time compute to improve capability. However, we observe that doing so increases latency, token usage, and FLOPs while yielding uneven, often diminishing gains in downstream success, limiting where embodied agents can be deployed. We argue that choosing when and where to spend test-time compute is central to bringing frontier performance to the real world. We introduce DIRECT, a routing framework that uses multimodal scene context to allocate compute per prompt, improving the success--cost Pareto frontier over fixed model selection. Across three dominant scaling axes, namely chain-of-thought depth, model size, and memory history, our experiments on VLABench and RoboMME show that test-time compute is not a uniform lever: different axes yield qualitatively distinct capability gains. We validate these insights on a physical Franka arm in a DROID setup spanning zero-shot manipulation and long-horizon chaining, where our router matches or exceeds a stronger model's success rate at up to 65% lower average latency. Ultimately, our results show that naively scaling test-time compute is wasteful, and that DIRECT can provide frontier-level embodied planning in robotic systems at a fraction of the cost. Project page can be found at jadee-dao.github.io/direct/.
